decisive_items: brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma
no conjunctival hyperemia, no discharge, and no epithelial defect
response.rationale: Deep stromal brown multilobular infiltrates without epithelial defect or inflammation are classic for fungal keratitis, especially after endothelial keratoplasty and corticosteroid use. Prior pine processionary infection resolved before surgery and is not an active cause; Acanthamoeba typically has ring infiltrate and severe pain, absent here.

rejected.why: Prior infection documented resolved before surgery; presentation is new keratitis, not recurrence of the same organism.
Immune-mediated keratitis is less specific and does not explain the distinctive deep brown multilobular lesions.
Acanthamoeba usually has epithelial/radial neuritis and pain; here no epithelial defect and deep lesions favor fungal.
Steroid-induced keratitis is not a recognized cause of this deep stromal infiltrate pattern.
Bacterial keratitis typically has epithelial defect and purulent exudate, absent here.
